abstract: Topological invariants constrain a driven Floquet generator, yet whether they protect a transient nonlinear bosonic resource remains open. We track boundary Wigner negativity of an even cat state in a chiral Floquet Su--Schrieffer--Heeger chain with boundary Kerr nonlinearity and structured loss. The quasienergy windings remain quantized at every chain length, yet the matched sector contrast flips sign when the chain grows under index-end shielding and is null within $3\times 10^{-5}$ under uniform loss at $t=T$ for $d\le 0.5$. Prepared and shielded on the physical dangling end, the contrast remains positive, modulated by local dimer return rather than set by the invariant. A three-site causal light cone and a boundary-Laplacian erosion law trace the flip to strong-bond bulk exposure: the sign is set by where the bulk-rate loss sits relative to the prepared site, not by chain length. We call this decoupling the resource--invariant gap.
